discovery: Rydberg blockade and programmable arrays of individually trapped Rydberg atoms for quantum simulation and quantum information processing

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire Charles Fabry, Institut d'Optique, CNRS, Université Paris-Saclay, France

motivation: The nominees made the strong dipolar interaction between Rydberg atoms a precise tool for engineering many-body quantum states one atom at a time. Lukin co-proposed the dipole-blockade mechanism and fast neutral-atom gates. Saffman demonstrated blockade between two individually trapped atoms and the first neutral-atom entangling gate. Browaeys pioneered optical-tweezer arrays of single atoms, reconfigurable assembly of defect-free arrays, and direct observation of coherent Rydberg excitation exchange. Building on this, the Browaeys and Lukin groups built programmable simulators with hundreds of atoms. These machines observed quantum phase transitions, topological spin liquids and quantum many-body scars, and Lukin's group demonstrated logical qubits with error detection. This decades-long programme turned isolated, controlled quanta into an experimental platform for strongly correlated quantum matter. Like cavity QED, it combines conceptual clarity with exquisite control of single quantum systems.
